affiliations.date_precision: The identifier-matched Army record dated 17 February 1943 carries civilian-occupation value 530; actual work dates, employer and relationship to OSS service are unestablished.

affiliations.occupation: Chauffeur or driver (bus, taxi, truck, or tractor)
affiliations.date_precision: The identifier-matched Army record dated 11 July 1942 carries civilian-occupation value 736; actual work dates, vehicle type, employer and relationship to OSS service are unestablished.
affiliations.research_notes: The Army row omits the printed Jr. suffix, but the exact private identifier establishes the match. The occupation category identifies neither a vehicle type nor an employer.

affiliations.role_title: Professor of political science; department chair, 1940-1948
affiliations.date_precision: Northwestern's archival description says Colegrove joined the faculty in 1919, became a full professor in 1926, chaired political science from 1940 to 1948 and retired in 1952; it dates his OSS consultancy to 1943-1945.
affiliations.research_notes: The university appointment demonstrably preceded and overlapped the 1943-1945 OSS consultancy. It is the best-supported immediate and last civilian affiliation currently documented; the evidence does not say Colegrove left Northwestern to join OSS.

affiliations.date_precision: The identifier-matched Army record dated 13 February 1943 carries civilian-occupation value 992; the institution, course and relationship to OSS service are unestablished.
affiliations.research_notes: Student status is not employment. No school, college, university, subject or degree is inferred from the coded category or separate education field.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Kenneth Colegrove is identified at high confidence as Northwestern political scientist Kenneth Wallace Colegrove, an OSS consultant from 1943 to 1945.
claims.evidence_excerpt: consultant to the U.S. Office of Strategic Services (O.S.S.) from 1943 to 1945
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Northwestern's archival description gives the full name, academic chronology and explicit OSS consultant dates for the unusually named Kenneth Colegrove.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The uncommon exact first-and-last-name match is joined to explicit OSS service by the subject's own university archives; the source index has no conflicting identifier or rank.
claims.temporal_assessment: The institutional description dates OSS consultancy to 1943-1945 and Northwestern employment from 1919 to retirement in 1952.
claims.match_notes: The match does not reach confirmed because the institutional description is not a direct Box 134 personnel-file linkage.

claims.claim_text: Kenneth Colegrove's best-supported immediate pre-OSS affiliation was Northwestern University, where he was a political science professor and department chair.
claims.evidence_excerpt: joined the Northwestern faculty in 1919, chaired the political science department from 1940 to 1948
claims.evidence_paraphrase: Northwestern places Colegrove continuously on its faculty from 1919 to 1952, including as department chair when his 1943-1945 OSS consultancy began.
claims.identity_match_assessment: The same institutional sources directly connect the uncommon exact name to both Northwestern and OSS.
claims.temporal_assessment: The employment began decades before and overlapped the OSS consultancy; no intervening affiliation is documented. This is strongly date-bounded rather than an explicit recruited-from statement.
claims.match_notes: The evidence supports a continuing academic employer, not a claim that Colegrove left Northwestern when he became an OSS consultant.

claims.temporal_assessment: The continuous appointment makes Northwestern the latest documented civilian employer before the OSS role; no military entry or intervening employer has been identified.
